summary: The review-flexibility PRD is ready for approval. It defines three coordinated changes: (1) task config becomes an ordinary editable input — the byte-pinning and config-digest-in-fingerprint enforcement is removed so mid-project edits never fail the workflow; changes are reported field-level in status and gate views instead, with existing per-dispatch route provenance as the durable record of what actually ran. (2) The existing per-dispatch reviewer route override becomes reachable through the semantic workflow tools, with outage guidance added to the skills, and the config template documents the per-phase-kind overrides section. (3) Human approval becomes a targeted trigger rather than a built-in default: counter-review stays machine-enforced before every step completes, while approval gates (PRD, design, commit) fire only when per-project rules match — subject triggers (prd/design) or content triggers (e.g. SQL file paths, presented with locations and change summaries). Default shipped ruleset: review PRD, review design, human approval for SQL file changes; commits are not gated (feature-branch + squash-merge workflow). Exception/safety gates (attempt exhaustion, constitution rule failure, drift, restore collisions, baseline adoption, migration audit) survive unchanged. Trigger rules live in per-project repository configuration, not constitution files, so rule changes inherit free editing with change reporting; the repo's own constitution is amended once to narrow the explicit-human-authority rule to triggered gates. A first counter-review raised three findings (config digest's role in the input fingerprint, gate-kind scope ambiguity, rule location vs constitution pinning); all three were accepted and folded into the revised PRD, and the fresh counter-review of the revised bytes returned no findings. One open decision to confirm at approval: trigger rules in repo config rather than constitution rule files — chosen for consistency with free editing; say so if you prefer constitution residency instead.
